inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 (ended 2026-08-31) = 9M actual $1,841.6M (Q3 10-Q) + Q4 at the top of the reaffirmed $2.45-2.47B guidance (~$626M; management said tracking to the high end). FY2026 actuals report 2026-09-30, two days after this build; refresh base_revenue and last_fcf then.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page shares outstanding 35,565,543 at 2026-06-25 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q) plus 0.07M dilutive securities (Q3 diluted 36.191M less basic 36.122M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. Actual count is shrinking ~5%/yr on buybacks, which is upside the flat-count convention does not credit.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q3 FY2026 10-Q (2026-05-31): LongTermDebt $1,389.7M = noncurrent $890.5M + current $499.2M (the $500M 2027 notes moved current); cash $288.1M. The Metrics.csv total_debt of $1,888.9M for this date double-counts the current portion on top of LongTermDebt and should be corrected via make fix.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow ShareBasedCompensation: 9M FY2026 $61.5M (Q1 18.5, Q2 20.9, Q3 22.2) + Q4 at the Q3 run-rate ~$22.5M = ~$84M FY2026E; FY2025 actual $61.2M. No PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag since FY2022 ($6.2M then), so no withholding is added; sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc, a small understatement (~$7M/yr if the FY2022 ratio held).
inputs.fcf_note: reported_fcf FY2026E = 9M OCF $617.5M less 9M capex $87.3M = $530.2M, plus Q4 at ~$179M (Q4 FY2025 was $178.2M; Q3 is the seasonal peak on annual billings). Owner FCF = 709 - 84 SBC - 0 interest income = 625. FY2025 actual owner FCF was 617.5 - 61.2 = 556.2.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $6.5M, 9M FY2026 $2.6M. Not stripped: the company is net DEBT ($1.1B), so no cash pile is added to EV and there is nothing to double-count.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 repurchases $506.0M (FY2025 $300.5M). Flat count is funded and then some; buybacks are value-neutral in this model because SBC is already deducted.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (Friday); FY2026 results are due before the open on 2026-09-30, so the price is likely to gap on the print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.2% (10y UST, Sept 2026) + beta 0.9 x 5.0% ERP = 8.7% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (5.2% 2027 notes, term loan at SOFR+), 4.0% after tax; weights ~88% equity ($9.7B market cap) / 12% debt ($1.39B) -> 8.1%, used as 8.0% in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the scenario paths and weights, not in per-scenario WACCs).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (office space) stay inside EBITDA as an operating expense under US GAAP presentation; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1: subscription data/software operating company, US filer, USD flows, no leases in the bridge, no NCI, no dual currency; owner-fcf-adaptations.md does not apply). EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC (SBC is charged separately via sbc_pct_path): FY2025 actual pre-SBC EBITDA (906.0 + 61.2)/2321.7 = 41.7%; FY2026E ~39.8% (9M GAAP operating income $543.3M, 29.5% margin, compressed by second-half-weighted AI investment; adjusted operating margin guided 34.0-35.5% vs ~37% in FY2025). D&A 9M FY2026 $133.7M = 7.3% of revenue, of which roughly 2.5-3pp is acquired-intangible amortisation (CUSIP Global Services 2022 asset purchase, tax-deductible over 15 years, so the tax shield is real). Capex 9M FY2026 $87.3M = 4.7% of revenue, mostly capitalised internal-use software. Cash taxes FY2025 $103.2M (~14% of pretax) vs FY2024 $157.0M (~24%); two-year average ~19%, effective GAAP rate ~17-18% (FDII, R&D credit) -> cash tax on EBIT ramps 18% to 20%. Working capital: deferred revenue is only ~7% of revenue and rose $8M on $119M of revenue growth in FY2025; receivables grow with revenue, so net capture set to 3% of the revenue change. Horizon 10 years: margins are near mature but FY2026 is an investment trough, so a 5-year build would capitalise a still-recovering margin. Terminal: max(0, min(Gordon, cap x FCF_N)), cap 20x base/bull, 15x bear. FY2026 is an estimate (9M actual + Q4 at guidance); update base_revenue, last_fcf, sbc and the balance-sheet anchors after the 2026-09-30 10-K.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 base-year growth set at 6.0%: organic ASV grew 7.1% at Q3 FY2026 and FY2026 revenue growth is ~6.3% at the top of guidance; the 8.0% 3-yr revenue CAGR includes the March-2022 CUSIP Global Services acquisition and is not an organic rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (18.0% 3-yr, 19.5% 5-yr) diverges >30% from revenue (8.0%/9.2%) and EPS (14.5%/9.9%). Book value compounded because buybacks were suspended in FY2022-23 to repay CGS acquisition debt ($18.6M FY2022 vs $250-350M/yr before); it is a capital-allocation artefact, not a growth signal, and is NOT used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs measured FY2022->FY2025 (3-yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5-yr) on the FY2025 10-K actuals; FY2026 is excluded as an estimate. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less cash-flow SBC; interest income not stripped because the company has carried net debt since FY2022 and pre-FY2022 net cash was well under 1x FCF): owner FCF 391.6 (FY20), 448.8 (FY21), 431.1 (FY22), 522.7 (FY23), 551.2 (FY24), 556.2 (FY25). Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR 8.9% is ABOVE the reported 8.2% because SBC grew slower than cash flow over FY2022-25 (56.0 -> 61.2); the 5-yr owner CAGR 7.3% is slightly below reported 7.6% because SBC rose faster over FY2020-25 (36.6 -> 61.2). FY2026 reverses this: SBC is running ~+37% (84 vs 61) on ~6% revenue growth, which is why sbc_pct_path starts at 3.6% not the 2.6% FY2025 level.

base.narrative: Organic ASV growth settles in the 5.5-6% range as AI-augmented upsell and enterprise contract restructuring offset modest seat attrition; pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2026 investment trough (39.8%) to 42% by FY2031, still below a return to the FY2025 peak-plus-expansion that management once implied. SBC stays elevated at 3.5% of revenue under the new CEO's equity-heavy plan before drifting to 3%.

bull.narrative: AI is net accretive: the Q3 FY2026 7.1% organic ASV print is the start of a re-acceleration to 8% as clients on FactSet AI solutions (growing ASV ~50% faster) become the majority of the book, Google Gemini agents and the Claude data connector make FactSet the audited data layer for agentic finance, and wealth/CTS outgrow the desktop. Investment spend normalises after FY2027 and operating leverage takes the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 44.5%.

bear.narrative: The AI-disruption thesis is right, just early: LLM tools commoditise data retrieval and screening, seat counts shrink at renewal even as retention stays above 95% (fewer seats per client, not fewer clients), Bloomberg and LSEG outspend FactSet in the AI arms race and price compression arrives on multi-year enterprise renewals. Nominal revenue stalls after FY2028 while defensive AI spend and data-licensing inflation grind the pre-SBC EBITDA margin down to 35%. Sell-side ASV (~18%) adds cyclical downside on a capital-markets slowdown. No solvency risk: net debt ~1.2x EBITDA.

scenario_narratives.base: ASV growth 5.5-6% fading to 3% over a decade; margin recovers to 42% pre-SBC by FY2031; SBC 3.5% of revenue; 20x FCF terminal cap at 2.5% growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-led re-acceleration to 8% ASV growth with operating leverage to a 44.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin; 3% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural seat erosion from LLM tools: revenue flat from FY2028, margin down to 35%, 1% terminal growth, 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the AI-commoditisation thesis is a credible structural (not cyclical) risk that already halved the stock in 2026, and the FY2026 margin compression shows management is spending to defend. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs two independent things to go right, durable ASV re-acceleration above 7% AND margin expansion beyond the FY2025 peak, while the smaller-scale-than-Bloomberg/LSEG constraint is permanent. Base 50%: the reaffirmed high-end FY2026 guidance and 95%+ retention make a mid-single-digit compounding path the central case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: FactSet is valued as a mature, high-retention subscription compounder on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC (now 3.4% of revenue and rising) is expensed, the share count is held flat, the FY2026 investment-trough margin is rebuilt from components rather than carried forward, and the CGS-inflated historical CAGRs are replaced by the organic ASV run-rate. The central question is whether AI erodes or entrenches the seat, and it is expressed in the growth and margin paths, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/LLM commoditisation of data retrieval shrinks seats per client at renewal; retention above 95% can coexist with falling ASV per client
FY2026 adjusted operating margin guided down to 34-35.5% on AI investment; if the spend becomes permanent the base-case margin recovery to 42% pre-SBC does not happen
SBC running ~37% above FY2025 under the new CEO's plan; every 1pp of revenue in SBC is ~$25M/yr of owner FCF
Sell-side ASV (~18%) is cyclical with investment-banking headcount
Acquisition cadence (Irwin, LiquidityBook) is rising: cash acquisitions are not in the FCF path and would reduce net cash generation
FY2026 base year is an estimate two days before the 10-K; base_revenue, last_fcf, SBC and the balance sheet should be refreshed on 2026-09-30
Terminal value is the majority of EV at an 8% WACC; the 20x cap on a 2.5% Gordon is what bounds it
